name: Vertex AI Vector Search
aliases: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Vector Search
tagline: Google Cloud's managed ANN service built on ScaNN, now part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
description: Vertex AI Vector Search, originally Matching Engine, is Google Cloud's managed approximate nearest neighbour service built on Google Research's ScaNN algorithm, the same technology behind Google Search and YouTube retrieval. You build indexes from embeddings in Cloud Storage or stream updates, deploy them to endpoints backed by provisioned nodes, and query dense, sparse or hybrid vectors with namespace restricts and numeric filters. Google has folded Vertex AI into the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and renamed the newer collection-based Vector Search 2.0 to Agent Retrieval, with auto-generated embeddings and reranking. Best for GCP-native teams with large, high-QPS workloads; minimum node costs make it pricey for small ones.

pricing.notes: Billed for node-hours of deployed index endpoints plus index build/update data processed. Google cites minimal setups under $100/month; shard count rises with dataset size and filters.

scale.notes: Indexes shard across nodes and autoscale replicas; billions of vectors at high QPS are supported.

queryLanguages: Vector Search API (restricts and numeric filters)
strengths: ScaNN delivers excellent recall/latency at billion scale
Streaming index updates for fresh data
IAM, VPC Service Controls and CMEK integration
Tight integration with Gemini embeddings and agent tooling
weaknesses: Provisioned nodes mean a baseline cost even when idle
Two generations (1.0 indexes vs Agent Retrieval collections) and renames cause confusion
Metadata filtering is less expressive than in Qdrant or Weaviate
notIdealFor: Small or spiky workloads on a budget
